points.quote: Theia plugins are handled in `plugin-ext/src/hosted/node/scanners/backend-init-theia.ts`. VS Code extensions are handled in `plugin-ext-vscode/src/node/plugin-vscode-init.ts`. It reuses the Theia API and overrides a few members. (headless plugins also mentioned; no runtime install/removal stated)
Plugins don't run inside Theia's main process. They run in an isolated host... the Theia backend forks a separate Node process... Browser-side plugins run in a web worker
The API is declared in `packages/plugin/src/theia.d.ts`. ... VS Code extensions are handled in `plugin-ext-vscode/src/node/plugin-vscode-init.ts`. It reuses the Theia API
In Node, module loading is overridden so that `import 'vscode'` or `import '@theia/plugin'` returns that object. ... In a web worker, the API is assigned to `window['theia']`.

Each side holds a proxy to the other, built from a paired interface. Pairs include `LanguagesMain` and `LanguagesExt` in `plugin-ext/src/common/plugin-api-rpc.ts`. Methods that can be called over RPC start with `$`.
For each connected frontend, the Theia backend forks a separate Node process... In the normal (non-headless) case the Theia backend only relays the messages.
Functions and object references can't. For those, the creating side caches the object and sends a handle (an id)... Messages are encoded with msgpackr.
Headless plugins get one shared backend host process. It isn't tied to any frontend. ... Main is the code in the browser frontend, or in the Node backend for headless plugins.
